Give every page a unique title and description that say what the page is about.
 Use one main heading per page, and headings that describe the sections below them.
 Add alt text to images that describes them.
 Make sure the site has a sitemap and isn't blocking search engines.
 For a local business, put your name, address and phone number in the same form everywhere.

## Step 7: Connect your domain and publish

Buy a domain (or use one you own), connect it to the builder, and check the site loads over HTTPS. Most builders walk you through the DNS records; our guide to connecting a custom domain explains them. After publishing, submit your sitemap to Google Search Console so the pages get crawled.

## Building it with Greta.sh [...] Greta.sh builds its own database for the site it generates; it does not plug into an existing production database. For marketing pages specifically, our guide to Greta.sh templates for marketers has landing page, funnel and quiz starting points.

## Mistakes to avoid

 Prompting with one line. "Make me a bakery website" gets a generic bakery website. Use the template in Step 3.
 Publishing the placeholder copy. Visitors notice, and invented claims can mislead customers.
 Choosing a page builder for an app's job. If customers need accounts or the site must store orders, start with a tool that builds a database.
 Forgetting the phone. Check every page at phone width before you publish.
 Treating launch as the finish line. Sites that get found keep adding useful pages.

People find websites through AI answers as often as search results now. A site that neither ranks on Google nor gets mentioned by AI assistants is invisible twice. A Self-growing Website works both fronts, on a schedule you approve. No content calendar, no agency.

### What is a self-growing website?

A website that keeps growing after it goes live. Greta builds and publishes the site, then researches your site and the sources you pick, and suggests new articles, pages and fixes.
